alex: Heads up — canary started throwing OOMs after the kernel-routing tweak this morning. Repro is pretty consistent on conv-heavy traces with variable batch shapes. nvtx trace attached, mem summary below. Anyone seen this pattern?

alex: ```
mem_total: 16384 MB
used: 15232 MB
free: 1152 MB
top_allocs:
  workspace: 9856 MB
  kv_cache: 4288 MB
  temp: 1088 MB
allocator knobs: expandable_segments=true, max_split_size_mb=32, garbage_collection_threshold=0.8
stack: serving/runtime -> kernel-router v2 -> kernel-selection: fused-conv-path
```

jamie: ugh. that kernel-routing change increases prefetch window for some fused kernels, so ws spikes. with expandable_segments=true segments grew but didn't shrink fast enough. frag + high GC threshold = late collection -> OOM :thinking_face: 

kevin: agree. two quick experiments that usually help: lower garbage_collection_threshold to ~0.5 so GC runs earlier, and increase max_split_size_mb to reduce split churn (try 128). small risk: larger splits can increase internal waste but reduces fragmentation in our workload.

maria: can we reproduce locally? if so i can run a knob sweep. also consider a transient compaction pass after large-batch requests. we have a compact-slabs path we can toggle.

alex: repro command (local): `./tools/run_local_repro --model gpt-conv-demo --batch-variance --profile nsight --duration 300`
trace: https://internal/traces/1765504321/oom-run1 (nvtx and mem timeline).

deploy-bot: canary-rollout: detected 5% increase in OOMs on cluster pool-a. rolling back routing->v1 for affected nodes. rollback id: 1765504000.

jamie: starting a quick A/B on a 4xA100 canary: set `garbage_collection_threshold=0.5` and `max_split_size_mb=128`, keep `expandable_segments=true` for now to see shrink behavior. will run 2h. i'll push flags with `rwctl runtime set-knobs --name canary-a --knobs garbage_collection_threshold=0.5,max_split_size_mb=128`

kevin: if that stabilizes, next step is to instrument the allocator to emit a "frag ratio" metric (free_small_chunks / total_free) so our autoscaler/optimizer can decide compaction. also add a cheap path: if predicted ws > 0.8 * free_mem, proactively trigger GC+compact.

maria: note from earlier experiments: bumping max_split_size_mb to 256 reduced fragmentation but caused a ~3% tail latency regression on short-chat workloads (large contiguous chunk allocation cost). saved logs at: https://internal/logs/alloc-sweep/2025-11-21-maxsplit-256.log

alex: thanks — i'll try the 0.5/128 combo on the canary that's still up and monitor nvtx and allocator histograms. will also test toggle `expandable_segments=false` to force earlier reclaiming in a controlled run.

jamie: quick status: after 45m with 0.5/128 on canary-a, no OOMs and mem headroom looks stable (~1.6GB free). I'll let it run full window then report. :thumbsup:

kevin: if this pattern repeats, propose we add a small runtime heuristic: when kernel-router switches a request to a higher-ws kernel, temporarily lower GC threshold and mark KV cache as lower-priority for eviction for N seconds. avoids immediate perf churn but prevents OOM.

maria: FYI adding auto compaction has compute cost; we'll need SRE signoff for CPU/time budget if we want it enabled platform-wide.

alex: cool. i'll post reproduction artifacts and a short checklist for oncall (knob quickfix + rollback steps) once jamie finishes the run.

jamie: finishing run now, uploading artifacts. tl;dr: gc=0.5 + max_split=128 looks promising on conv-heavy traces. next: benchmark tail-latency impact on chat workloads.

kevin: nice. follow-up ticket idea: allocator should expose eviction pressure events so both kernel-router and autoscaler can react. created ephemeral issue in backlog.

deploy-bot: note: rollback completed for nodes with ID prefix pool-a-7.

alex: thanks all, assigning next steps in the triage doc and linking the reproducer.
